payload.name: ExtractPerMemberAttributesFromEnumerations
payload.description: When a message assigns separate attributes to multiple distinct members of a group using names, ordinals, or other identifiers, extract one memory candidate per member during construction.
content: During candidate extraction, if a user enumerates distinct members of a group and gives each a different quality (e.g., 'oldest is...', 'second is...', 'youngest is...'), create a separate candidate for each member, preserving the member identifier in the memory text.
Do not merge the enumeration into one generic memory such as 'all members have personalities' and do not skip it because the group is informal or unnamed.
For each candidate, store the specific attribute as a stable profile fact about that member and include enough context (e.g., 'oldest pet', 'second child') to distinguish it from other members.

solves: A construction pass can silently drop an explicit per-member enumeration ('oldest is relaxed, second is playful') by treating it as one anecdote. This rule forces one memory candidate per enumerated member so each attribute is preserved. Applies whenever a message labels distinct entities and assigns each its own attribute; not when the group is described only collectively.
